events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Is Born in Corsica
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Ajaccio, Corsica, the second of eight children in a modest island family. He rose through the French army during the Revolution and became Emperor of the French.
events.significance: Napoleon reshaped European politics, law and warfare. His Napoleonic Code still influences legal systems around the world.

events.title: The Panama Canal Opens to Traffic
events.description: The cargo ship SS Ancon made the first official transit of the Panama Canal. The passage connected the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans through Central America.
events.significance: The canal cut thousands of miles off sea routes and changed global trade and shipping. It is still one of the world's most important waterways.

events.title: Japan Announces Its Surrender
events.description: Emperor Hirohito broadcast Japan's surrender to the Japanese people, bringing World War II to its effective end. The day is remembered as Victory over Japan Day. It is also the day Korea was freed from Japanese rule.
events.significance: The broadcast ended the deadliest war in history. It also began Japan's postwar transformation and led to Korea's liberation, which is still marked each year.

events.title: India Gains Independence From Britain
events.description: After nearly 190 years of British company and crown rule, India became independent and joined the Commonwealth of Nations. Jawaharlal Nehru took office as the country's first Prime Minister.
events.significance: Independence ended the British Raj and began the end of colonial empires in Asia and Africa. India now celebrates August 15 as its national Independence Day.

events.title: Woodstock Music & Art Fair Opens
events.description: The Woodstock Music & Art Fair opened in Bethel, New York, with some of the top rock musicians of the era. It became one of the defining gatherings of the 1960s counterculture.
events.significance: Woodstock became a lasting symbol of the music and ideals of a generation. It remains a landmark in the history of popular culture.
